highlights: Atlantis for Linux and Windows: a `.deb`, an `.rpm` and an AppImage for x64 Linux, and an installer for x64 Windows, beside the Mac app.
The Mac app needs macOS 11 Big Sur or later.

items: `just release beta`, `alpha`, `stable` or `patch` is the whole release. It works out the next version, asks for a codename, a line for the site and the release notes (from the changelog, generated from the commits since the last tag, or your own), then commits and tags the release and drafts it on atlantis-web. atlantis-web's new Release workflow builds macOS, Linux and Windows, attaches every package and only then publishes the release and updates the site. `just publish`, `scripts/publish.sh` and this repo's manual `Package` workflow are gone.
atlantis-web keeps the newest stable release hosted past the newest three, so a run of betas leaves stable users something to download.

The Intel half of the Mac app said it ran on macOS 10.13, but whisper.cpp needs 10.15 for `std::filesystem`, so it would not have started on 10.13 or 10.14. `minimumSystemVersion` is now `11.0` in `tauri.conf.json`, the floor Apple Silicon already had, and the build no longer depends on a newer Xcode quietly allowing it.

The Linux build compiles again. `tauri-plugin-deep-link` 2.6.2 fills in `rust-ini`'s `ParseOption` field by field, and `rust-ini` 0.21.2 added fields to it, so `Cargo.lock` holds `rust-ini` at 0.21.1.

highlights: Type `/` and a skill's name in a chat, like `/grill-me my plan`, and the agent follows that skill for the request.

Six new providers: OpenAI, ChatGPT on your plan, Anthropic, OpenRouter, OpenCode Go and Ollama on your own machine. A custom provider can speak OpenAI Chat Completions, which covers Groq, DeepSeek, LM Studio and most others.
Every model is rated out of 10 for how strong it is, from the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, and you can rate one yourself.
Talk to your agents and hear them answer. What you say is written down by Whisper on your own machine unless you pick a provider, and each agent can have a voice of its own.
Agents in the Garage reply to one another the way people in a group chat do, rather than claiming a message and debating it.

The Oracle's house is three times the size, on an island of its own, with room for many more agents. There is a two-storey office, glass meeting rooms, a music room, a pool, a basketball court, a football pitch, and a tall ship moored off the dock to board.
Keep your library on another computer or a NAS on your home or office network, and every agent reads it from there, with nothing copied over.

items: Type `/` and a skill's name in a chat, like `/grill-me my plan`, and the agent follows that skill for the request. Any skill the agent has works this way, its own or a common one, including the ones it only uses when asked.
An agent stands in its own chat, full height behind the thread, breathing, blinking and looking at you, dressed and shaped the way its Appearance tab says.

OpenCode Go as a provider. Paste the key from the OpenCode console, or export `OPENCODE_API_KEY`, and every Go model is listed. Each runs over the API its maker speaks, except Gemini, which Atlantis cannot run yet.
OpenAI as a provider, billed to an API key from the OpenAI platform or `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

ChatGPT as a provider. `Sign in with ChatGPT` on its Config tab signs in through the browser, and turns are billed to your plan's included usage, within the limit set for Atlantis in ChatGPT settings. Sign out ends the session with OpenAI too.
OpenCode Go and OpenAI models show their context size and what they can do, read from models.dev, so a long conversation is not cut to a few thousand tokens.

Ollama on your own machine as a provider, with no key. Every model you have pulled is listed, and a turn runs at a 32k window, or the model's own when it is smaller, so Ollama no longer drops the start of a long conversation.

OpenRouter as a provider. `Sign in with OpenRouter` makes a key labelled Atlantis without leaving the app, or paste one or export `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. Every model shows its context size and what it can do.
Anthropic as a provider, billed to an API key from the Claude platform or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Every Claude model shows its context size and what it can do.
`atlantis://` links bring Atlantis to the front, which is what the Back to Atlantis button on the sign-in page does.
Remove a provider with the trash in its sheet's head. The first press asks, and says which agents will be left without a model.

A custom provider can speak OpenAI Chat Completions, which covers Groq, Together, Fireworks, DeepSeek, Mistral, LM Studio, vLLM and most others. Give it the base URL its docs give, and its models are read from `/models`.

The Oracle's library follows its folder as it changes. A page added, removed, retitled or retagged in the wiki moves on the shelves while you are in the house, and Tron's Library tab updates its counts.

A wiki with a topic tree, every page carrying `topics`, is shelved by its topics on the library's ground floor, each named by its topic page, and the largest topic goes up to the gallery. Pages without a topic go by their tags as before, up in the gallery.
The library's shelves fill from the right, the end nearest the door, on both floors.
Ask the library's keeper about the page you're reading with the speech bubble beside Close. It opens their chat with the page attached, and your next message tells them which page it's about.

A working desk in the library, under the gallery by the glass, holds what the wiki has open in four stacks: open questions, pages in flight, what to research next, and what needs you (open reviews, pages sent back, and the inbox). Click a book to read it.

Every model shows how strong it is, out of 10, where 10 is the strongest model available today and every other model is rated by its share of that model's score on the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, whoever made it. The flames burn yellow to 3, green to 6, red to 8, blue at 9 and black and white at 10, beside each model on the Models page, in the model select and on the agent's model pill.
Rate a model yourself, or correct its rating, with the flames on an agent's model card. Press your rating again, or `Use`, to go back to Atlantis's.

An agent's model card says what its model can be trusted with at that rating, from everyday chores to the hardest problems, and links to the model leaderboard on the site, where every rating and the benchmarks behind it are.
Tron's About tab links to the model leaderboard, beside Privacy and Terms.

Talk to your agents. The microphone beside send, in every chat and the Garage, records until you press it again and writes what you said into the message, ready to read over before Enter. Esc throws a recording away.

Hearing runs on Whisper on your own machine by default, and nothing you say leaves it. Tron's new Voice tab downloads a Whisper model, from Tiny at 32 MB to Large v3 Turbo at 574 MB, and can send speech to OpenAI, OpenRouter or an OpenAI-compatible host like Groq instead.
Hear an agent's answer read aloud with the speaker under it, through OpenAI or OpenRouter. When you send a message you spoke, the answer is read aloud on its own, which the Voice tab can switch off.

Give each agent a voice of its own on the Voice tab of its sheet: thirteen voices to hear and pick from, and a few words on how it speaks, its pace, tone or accent. They are written into its `SOUL.md` under `## Speaking voice`, apart from `## Voice`, which is still how it writes.
Downloaded Whisper models show under Voice on the Storage tab, where they can be removed.
The Oracle's house is three times the size, with room for many more agents: 82 desks in the office, 28 seats in meeting rooms, 34 in the lounge, 22 in the kitchen and 24 in the game and music rooms.

The office is two storeys tall round an atrium, with a mezzanine up a floating stair. There are no rows of desks: each team has a section in its own colour and works round a round desk or a long shared one, with a computer at every place.
Meetings happen in four glass rooms for up to seven, one in each corner of the office, two on each floor.
A room of your own in the office's upstairs west corner, glass on two sides to the sea: dark, lit by neon, with a desk facing the view, a retro sunset print and an arcade cabinet.
The lounge has sofas round rugs, a reading nook by the window, magazine racks with the day's papers, a coffee bar, and pictures and screens on every wall.
The game room has table tennis, four arcade cabinets, two chess tables and a console with a sofa, beside the pool table.
The kitchen is a fitted kitchen, with units along two walls, a hob under a hood, a sink, an island with stools and two tables to eat at.
Tiki torches light the path down to the beach at night, and there are loungers and umbrellas on the sand, and tables to eat at.
Out in the sea, a rock with a cave at its foot and a lighthouse on top, its beams sweeping round at night.
The house stands on its own island, with a lawn round the house, a beach in front, palms along every shore and the sea in every direction.

Behind the house, an Olympic pool with lanes, starting blocks, and loungers and tables like the beach's, a basketball court with benches either side, and a full-size football pitch with stands all round it. The island is more than twice the size to hold them, and its coast is no longer straight: a cove at the front, bays and a sandy spit down the west and back, and a jagged east shore of rocks and boulders with sea stacks offshore. Palms grow all over it.
A music room off the game room, treated for sound with bass traps, absorbers and diffusers, with a grand piano, a drum kit, guitars, mics and speakers. Agents go there to play.
A chandelier hangs in the library, and every room has more lights, with picture lights over the lounge's paintings.
A tall ship is moored off the end of the dock with its sails furled. Walk out along the jetty and up the plank to board it, and go below to the gun deck, the hold and the captain's cabin.

Connect the library to a WebDAV server by its address, like `http://starkm1:8080/`, under From a server on Tron's Library tab. It is read straight off the server, never copied to disk and never written, and every agent reads it by that address. Any server that speaks WebDAV works: `rclone serve webdav`, Caddy's or nginx's WebDAV module, Apache's `mod_dav`, or a NAS.

The first look at a library on a server reads every page, which takes a few seconds for a large wiki over a slow link. After that only a page that changed is fetched again, and the shelves follow the server every 20 seconds.
An address with a name or password in it is refused, so for now the server has to serve the library without a login. A library on a server has no keeper, so the reader has no Ask button for it.

`library::Place`, where the library is kept: a folder or an address. `Settings.library` holds one, written as a single string, so a `settings.json` from before reads as the folder it named. `Place::parse` reads an `http://` or `https://` address as a server, ends its path in `/`, drops a query or fragment, and refuses a login with `AddressLogin`.

`library::remote::Remote`, a library on a WebDAV server. It lists the server at depth infinity when the server allows it, and a folder at a time, 16 at once, when it refuses, as Apache does by default. A listing is reused for 5 seconds. Each page is held in memory with the ETag its listing gave it and fetched again only when that moves. The catalogue and the page opener run over the listing and the held pages, note what they read that is not held, fetch it all together and run again.

`library::dav`, the `Dav` seam the shell implements with its client, the `PROPFIND` it sends, and the parser of the multistatus answer, which matches elements by local name and reads only a `200` propstat. `backend::Web` implements it.

`read_file`, `list_dir` and `search` read a library on a server by its address, through `Net::library`. A write to the library's address is refused as a shared folder, and `Home::resolve` refuses any other address as outside the home, so a write can no longer make an `http:` folder in a home.
Errors for a library on a server: `BadAddress`, `AddressLogin`, `LibraryUnreachable` and `NotWebDav`.

`crates/atlantis-app/tests/remote_library.rs`, ignored, reads a library off a real WebDAV server and checks it shelves exactly as the folder it serves, with request counts and timings. `LIBRARY_RTT_MS` adds a delay per request to stand in for a distant server.
Building Atlantis now takes cmake, for whisper.cpp.
Adding a provider opens it on its Config tab when it still needs a key or a sign-in, and its models are read once the key is saved.
Provider sheets are wider on a large window.
The agents rail lists the agent you last chatted with first. Agents you have never spoken to follow, in the order they were added.
Model lists on the Models page and in the model select read strongest first, then newest.

Agents in the Garage reply to one another the way people in a group chat do. Every post, yours or an agent's, is put to each agent that didn't write it, and those it warrants a reply from answer: when it's put to them, falls to them with something new to add, gets something in their area wrong, or says something they disagree with. Each agent listens on its own and replies whenever it's free, with no rounds holding anyone up, and a conversation runs until nobody has anything more to say. This replaces claiming a message and debating it, and there are no more notes about rounds or debates settling.
Set how many times each agent may reply to one Garage message under Tron's General tab, from 1 to 100. It is 20 unless changed.

Pick a model for Garage reply decisions under Tron's General tab. Every agent is asked about every post, so a small fast model keeps a busy Garage quick. Left unset, each agent decides with its own model.
An agent in the Garage that finds it has nothing to add passes, and nothing is posted, rather than saying the message is not theirs.
The microphone is disabled until voice input is set up: a Whisper model downloaded, or a provider picked that can transcribe and has a key or sign-in that works. Pointing at it says what is missing.
Agents answer in the Garage precisely, with the specifics that settle a question and without greetings or the question said back.

Runek 0.17.0. The Oracle's first person is much wider, about 140° across, through a gently curved lens that softens toward the edges, and the camera no longer shakes while you walk. A book on a shelf or on the working desk lights up and opens only once you are close enough to reach it. Palms grow fuller crowns, agents only turn their heads to you from nearby, and everything drawn from a seed comes out differently than before: the furniture, the palms and rocks, and any part of an agent's figure its `SOUL.md` does not describe. A gender or hair style you picked for your own figure stays as it is. The Oracle is cheaper to draw: parts that look alike share one material and are merged into a few draws, the house's 54 lights at night become a pool of ten given to the ones nearest you, shadows redraw 30 times a second rather than every frame, and the world renders at up to 1.5 times the screen's pixel density, stepping down while frames run slow.

The catalogue, the page opener and the working desk read through a `Shelf`, a folder or what a server answered, rather than the filesystem. A folder is read as before, but a symlink inside a library is no longer shelved: `open` already refused a page that resolved outside the folder, and the shelves now agree with it.
`Catalogue.root` is a string, the folder's path or the server's address.

`library`, `set_library`, `create_library` and `library_page` are async commands, and a folder is read on a blocking thread rather than the main one. `set_library` lists an address before keeping it, so a server that is not there, or not WebDAV, is refused with why.
Your figure in the Oracle stands on the floor in the views from behind and overhead, rather than a hand's width above it.

A library too big for the Oracle's shelves no longer leaves books off them. Every page is on a shelf, the crowded shelves draw their books thinner, and with more subjects than shelves the smallest share the General shelves.

notes: Group of Agents at your service

items: Following a link from one book in the library to another takes you to the shelf that book is on, upstairs or down, standing in front of it with its label in view. Back takes you to the shelf of the book before.

Start an LLM wiki of your own with New library under Tron's `Library` tab. Give it a name and a line on what it is about, and it is laid out with `raw/` for sources, `wiki/` for pages, an index, a log and a `CONVENTIONS.md` saying how pages are written, then connected as the library. A new librarian keeps it by default, living in the library's own folder so the whole thing opens as one Obsidian vault, or an agent you already have keeps it in a folder of its home. Either way the keeper gets skills to ingest a source, answer from the wiki and check it. A folder with anything in it is never written over.

The Oracle page is a house you can walk around in 3D, with an office, a conference room, a library, a kitchen, a lounge, a game room and the front door, and every agent lives in it. An agent mid-turn sits at a desk with the tool it is running over its head, one working in the Garage sits at the conference table, an offline one stands outside the front door saying why. The rest follow their needs: hungry after a lot of tokens, they go to the kitchen, and bored after a run of turns, they go to the game room, and come back to the lounge once they have eaten or played. They walk between rooms as that changes. WASD walks, the scroll wheel zooms, Shift and the scroll wheel tilt, on a trackpad too, and V changes the view. Beside an agent, T opens its chat over the house and I its sheet. The house takes the app's colours in both themes and replaces the empty watch list. It is `world.json` in the app's data folder, so it can be rearranged by editing it, and the Storage tab counts it under Settings.

You walk the house as a figure of your own. `Customise Avatar` under Tron's `Appearance` tab opens a studio with your figure on a turntable, where you choose a gender, a hair style and your clothes and roll a new face and build before saving. Agents dress for work.
The agent sheet shows an agent's energy, hunger and fun. Energy is how much of its context window is free.

Notifications, as lines in the logbook marked with a bell. A failed diagnostic check and anything an agent says in the Garage are notifications. Akashic Records has a `Notifications only` switch that shows them alone, at the level the slider is on.
A `notify` tool, so an agent can tell you something as a notification, like a long task finishing or a decision waiting on you, at the level it picks.
A startup sound, a short chime as Atlantis opens. Off by default, turned on under Tron's `Appearance` tab.

Pictures in an agent's home show in the chat, whether it writes the path out, as a Markdown image or as an Obsidian embed like `![[doodle.webp]]`. A path from inside a note, like `assets/doodle.webp`, is found too. PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, SVG, BMP, HEIC and ICO up to 8 MB, and nothing outside the agent's home is ever read.

Atlantis runs the full diagnostics while it starts, and the loading screen lists each check as it lands, with `ok`, `fail` or `skip`. The keychain asks for each provider's key there, once, so a conversation never stops mid-turn for it. When a check fails, the loading screen stays up and says what failed, with `Run again` and `Open anyway`. Tron's House tab opens on that run, and a failed check is a warning in the logbook.

Atlantis checks [atlantis.orionpod.com](https://atlantis.orionpod.com) for a newer build as it opens. When there is one, `Update` shows in green beside the version at the foot of the left sidebar, or a green dot on the collapsed rail, and opens that release on the download page. Nothing is downloaded or installed by itself.

An About tab in Tron, one card with the version and the machine it runs on, a `Check for updates` button beside it, what Atlantis is built with (orion-core, Runek, Tauri and WebKit), links to the website, Discord and the policies, and the author's Mastodon, X and GitHub.

`just version`, `just package`, `just publish` and `just release`, which release a build to [atlantis-web](https://github.com/anistark/atlantis-web) and update the site at [atlantis.orionpod.com](https://atlantis.orionpod.com). `just package` builds one universal app for Apple Silicon and Intel and puts it in a DMG with `hdiutil` alone. `just publish` tags the repo, attaches the DMG to a release on atlantis-web, keeps the newest three there and writes the release, with its changelog, into the site's release list.

Agents can ask each other for help. Every agent has an `Ask agent` tool that hands a task to any other agent that can answer and gets its answer back. The agent asked works with its own tools in its own home, its work shows under the call while you wait, and it shows as busy in the roster and at a desk in the Oracle. Each pair of agents keeps a conversation of its own, so a helper remembers what it was asked before, and every ask and answer is posted in the Garage. An agent asked for help cannot ask anyone further.

An agent can ask another in the background and carry on. When the answer lands, the asking agent replies to it in its chat without you sending anything, and the answer is a notification. An answer still out when Atlantis closes is lost, and the agent is told so on its next turn.
Notifications show as macOS banners, headed by the agent that sent them, and play a short sound. Each can be switched off: banners under Tron's `General` tab, the sound under `Appearance`.

An agent's `SOUL.md` can say how it looks, in a sentence under an `## Appearance` heading like `You are a tall, lean man, and you dress in a dark suit and tie.`, and the Oracle dresses and shapes its figure to match. Gender, build, height, clothes, skin colour, hair, hair colour and facial hair are read off the words, and whatever the file leaves out is the figure the agent always had. A change to the file shows the next time the Oracle opens, or after Read again.

An Appearance tab on the agent sheet, beside Skills, to choose how an agent looks without editing its `SOUL.md` by hand. The agent stands on a turntable that you drag to turn, with a row of choices each for height, age, gender, build, skin colour, hair, hair colour, facial hair and clothes, and `Any` leaves a part to the figure the agent always had. The sentence that will go under `## Appearance` shows above the choices as you pick, and Save writes it, leaving the rest of the file as it was.

New clothes to dress a figure in: a suit, a dark jacket and trousers of one cloth with a white shirt and a tie, a chic camel trench open over black with ankle boots and a bag, and a sage's robe and cloak with a staff. Hair can be medium, cut to the jaw, and a figure can be an elder, a little shorter and stooped.

How far one turn may go is set under Tron's `General` tab: the tool rounds, how many times a turn may go back to the model with a tool's answer, and the model call time, how long one call to a model may take.

The library reads any folder of Markdown, not only an LLM wiki in the Karpathy shape. A flat vault's notes, and any loose beside the folders, are shelved under Notes. Tags are read however a vault writes them, `tags: ml`, `tags: ml, evals`, `tag:`, `Tags:` or Obsidian's `#tags` in the text, and `ML` and `ml` are one subject. `.markdown` files are pages, folders named `inbox`, `review`, `config` or `campaigns` are read like any other, and a vault's `Templates` and `attachments` are left out. Agents are pointed at the library's `index.md` only when there is one.
A turn may take 200 tool rounds rather than 32, and a model call 3000 seconds rather than 120, unless set otherwise.

orion-core 0.8.0. Every tool takes a `ToolContext`, and a turn returns everything it added but what was typed, since the harness can now add messages ahead of it. `tokio` is a dependency of the shell rather than only of its tests.
About Atlantis in the menu bar shows the app's icon, the tagline, a link to the website and the copyright, and the version once rather than twice.
A dev run, `just dev`, skips the diagnostics on the loading screen, which shows them as `skip`. Dr. House still runs them when asked.
The typecheck is `tsc -b`, so the Runek components copied into `src/runek/` are checked under their own settings, in `tsconfig.runek.json`, and the app's stay as strict as before.
The Storage tab says how much of the disk is still free, `(234 GB usable)`, in green, or in yellow when it's under the 200 MB Dr. House warns about.
The House tab in Tron is called Dr. House.
Both sidebars start collapsed to their icon rails. Click a rail's mark to open it.
Dr. House's quick and full picker is headed `Diagnostics Centre` rather than `Scope`, and Run is a play button that turns into a locking reticle while the checks run.
The number of skills on the agent sheet's Skills tab is a pill, the way the sidebar counts its agents.
The Oracle opens in first person, facing the lounge. V still switches to the view from behind and the one from overhead.
`Customise Avatar` is disabled while the Oracle is in first person, where your figure is out of sight.
Tool rounds and model call time are sliders, stepping through set values from 1 to 1000 rounds and from 10 seconds to a day.
In the Oracle, an agent answers a question where it is, and only goes to a desk in the office once the turn has run for half a minute. The same goes for an agent helping another.
Each agent has a usual room it waits in while it wants for nothing: the lounge, the office, the conference room or the new library. Set it under Usual room when editing an agent.

Connect the library to a folder of Markdown, like an LLM wiki, under Tron's new `Library` tab. The Oracle's library takes its name, from its README or its folder, and shelves it like a real library, by subject read off each page's tags, with each shelf labelled with its subject and the letters it runs between, a book per page, and clicking a book, or the open book on the lectern, opens the page to read over the house, links and all. Every agent can read the library with its tools from its next turn, and is told where it is. The tab shows how many pages each section holds.

Every page has a pixel-art room behind it: a cyberpunk tech conference room for the Garage, an armory for the Armory, a cyber control centre for Tron and a file and analysis room for the Akashic Records. Each agent's chat gets a room for what it does, a library, a studio, a chamber, a lab or a study, in both themes.
Tron's settings sit on liquid glass, a frosted card with a frosted tile for each row.
The Oracle fills the whole window, with the sidebars and the title floating over the world like a HUD.
The Oracle opens where you left it: where you stood, the way you faced and the view you were in.

The Oracle's sky follows your own clock: a daylight sky with the sun moving across it, a sunset, and stars at night, with the light changing to match and the house's ceiling lights coming on as it gets dark.
The house is finished: full-height walls, open doors in every doorway, windows to the outside, and ceilings over the rooms and the library, which the overhead view still sees through.
The house looks out to sea: a green terrace with palms runs down to a wide beach, with a dock, sailboats on the open ocean, a campfire on the sand and rocky headlands either side of the cove.

The house has a round library off its west side, through a door beside the lounge sofa: a two-storey rotunda with a glass curtain wall, a gallery on columns reached by a grand stair, curved shelves on both floors with room for some 2,600 books, the library's name on the wall at the top of the stair, a clock that keeps your own timezone and names it, and couches and reading tables upstairs and down. Only the library's real pages are books.

Agents get lonely. A new Social need empties over an hour with no work and no break, and a lonely agent goes to the lounge for a few minutes before heading back. It shows on the agent sheet beside energy, hunger and fun.
A long robe, dress or coat in the Oracle no longer loses its front and sides toward the hem.
The loading screen is removed once it fades, instead of staying behind the app, invisible and still animating.

A reply where the agent wrote its tool call as XML tags, or made up the tool's answer after the call, no longer shows that markup. A call written that way that never ran shows as not run, like any other.
Opening a plugin from `Browse AgentHub` and coming back keeps the search and the `Skills`/`Everything` filter.
A plugin whose AgentHub entry points at a folder its repository no longer has says so, instead of that it carries no skills.
